approach: Add one module, crates/athena-core/src/followups.rs, and call it from one line of `Athena::close_dispatched` (run/close.rs:38), the only place a job that ran is closed. The module has four parts. (1) `is_follow_up(item)` matches whole-word directive phrases ('as its own job/request', 'as a follow-up request', 'propose ... follow-up') and never bare words. (2) `chain_root` walks the 'try again on <job>' retry link (`retried_job`, reading/retry.rs:201, the link `retry_target` follows at preflight.rs:300-329) to the first job of the chain. (3) A pure `queue(..)` queues nothing when any steward request in the records already carries an `Out-of-scope item key: <root> ` line. Otherwise it queues up to MAX_PER_JOB = 5 distinct directive items, each through the existing `RequestQueue::apply` on a `ProposedChange`, so `StewardRequest::new` (steward.rs:535) stays the only request-text builder. (4) `Athena::follow_up_files` loads Records at HEAD, calls `queue` and returns `NewFile`s, which are added to `closing.files` and go in the same closing commit as the outcome. There is no new record type, config key, crate or dependency. Round-3 changes: the 'item names an existing record id' skip is dropped (finding 2). Dedupe is per retry chain, not per item wording (finding 3). Files come from the item only, and the title is cut at a word boundary (finding 4). The lock claim is corrected (finding 5). The drain-turn side effect is named in the CHANGELOG and pinned by an `improvement_of` assertion (finding 6). manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are listed as deliverables but are not needed. manage.rs is only the person's `athena close` for jobs that did not finish (manage.rs:74, 82, 240), and steward.rs and reading.rs already supply everything reused.

decisions.choice: Hook in run/close.rs `close_dispatched`: one call line `closing.files.extend(self.follow_up_files(ctx.id(), ctx.reading, ctx.ui));` right after `push_closing_records(&mut closing);` (close.rs:38). run/close.rs is added to the file list; manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are left unedited, and the producer says so in its report. Answer to finding 1.
decisions.reason: The reading says manage.rs is where a job closes and the producer must confirm it. I confirmed it against the code. manage.rs `close` (74) and `close_with` (82) are the person's `athena close` for a job that did not finish (Queued or Proposed become Dropped, Declined or Blocked become Abandoned, an interrupted Dispatched job becomes Abandoned after `recover_interrupted`, 240). A job that ran closes only in `close_dispatched` (close.rs:8): the plain commit at close.rs:132 for rejected, failed and stale outcomes, and `land_or_block` (244) for landed and blocked ones. I looked for a listed file that could host the call and found none. `closing.files` is built in run/mod.rs (`Closing`, 121) and run/close.rs. The commit helpers are in commits.rs (110-257). lib.rs holds only `head()` (273). Any call from a listed file would still need a call site in close.rs, so one call line there is the smallest edit that reaches the fgwz case. The logic stays in followups.rs, and the scope is unchanged: queue follow-ups when a job ends with a reading. If a scope guard refuses the close.rs edit, the producer reports it and does not route around it.

rejected.option: Hook in manage.rs `close_with`, to stay inside the listed deliverables
rejected.why: It sees only jobs closed by hand, never a job that ran to an outcome, so criterion 1 (the fgwz case) would not hold. It would also queue work from jobs a person abandoned.

rejected.option: Hook inside commits.rs `commit_records_with` or `build_commit`
rejected.why: Those build every commit (asks, interventions, steward), not only a job's closing. It is also a file outside the list.

rejected.option: A steward scan that queues follow-ups for every closed job with a reading
rejected.why: It runs on a later pass, not when the job ends, and would backfill historical jobs including fgwz, which the brief puts out of scope.

rejected.option: Queue in a second records commit after the closing commit
rejected.why: The outcome could land without its follow-ups if the second commit fails. One commit is atomic.

decisions.choice: Drop the id-based 'filed elsewhere' skip. Whether an item is queued depends only on the directive matcher and the chain dedupe of decision 3. An item that cites any job or introspection id (for example 'Propose these as follow-up requests: closing 20261017-205552-y1bh and 20261030-060410-9e5h') is queued like any other. Answer to finding 2.
decisions.reason: Citing a record is the usual way to name work about it (close it, fix its findings), so a cited id does not mean the work is filed. The pj25 item of this brief is already kept out by the directive matcher: 'a separate request from introspection ...-pj25' has no 'as' before 'a separate' and no 'propose'. The ids stay in the request text as references only. `followed_up_ids` (topics.rs:479) reads an id only right after 'follow up', 'follow-up', 'followup', 'follows up' or 'following up', with only on, of, to, job, the, earlier between, so 'follow-up requests: closing <id>' is not read as a continuation. `dependency_ids_in` (topics.rs:25) reads only a 'Depends on' line, and `referenced_jobs` (topics.rs:533) shows at most 3 cited jobs to the reader and truncates the rest. The criterion 1 table and the end-to-end test now include fgwz-shaped items that cite existing ids and assert they are queued. The end-to-end test cites the id of a real job in its records, made with `athena.ask`.

rejected.option: Keep the skip for ids of jobs or introspections in the records
rejected.why: It drops real fgwz follow-ups, which cite jobs that exist, and the matcher already excludes the pj25 item.

rejected.option: Skip only on explicit wording such as 'already queued as <id>' or 'from introspection <id>'
rejected.why: No such wording is needed for any item of the brief or of fgwz. A second matcher is more refusal-like surface for no test-visible gain; a wrongly queued request is closed with `athena close`.

decisions.choice: Dedupe and cap per retry chain, not per item wording. `chain_root(records, closing)` loops at most 16 times: it reads the current job's `request.text`, calls `crate::reading::retried_job(records, text)`, and stops at a cycle, an unknown job or a request that is not 'try again on <job>', as `retry_target` does (preflight.rs:300-329). The text of each queued request holds a line `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> <n>`, where n is the item's number in the reading. `queue` returns an empty plan when any request on REQUEST_CHANNEL at HEAD has a line starting `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> `. Otherwise it queues the first MAX_PER_JOB = 5 distinct directive items; items beyond 5 are reported as skipped. Answer to finding 3.
decisions.reason: A retry (the drain's or a person's 'try again on <job>') gets a brand-new reading from a model whose out_of_scope wording drifts, so keys built from the item text would queue every item again. Once any request holds the chain's marker, later jobs of the chain queue nothing, whatever their wording. A re-close, a failed-then-retried job and a held-then-resumed job all see the marker. The hash of the earlier plan is gone because within one reading duplicates are dropped by comparing the normalised text in memory. The retry link is the 'try again on <job>' request text (reading.rs:1307 `RETRY_PREFIX`; `retry_reference`, retry.rs:560), not `previous_job`, which is the latest landed job (chain.rs:1; scope_guard.rs:639). The cost is that a retry whose reading adds a genuinely new follow-up queues none of it. This is accepted and named in risks. If the root job's own reading had no follow-up item, nothing carries its marker, so a later retry that has some still queues them, under the root's id. The test of criterion 3 now rewords the items on the retry, so it fails if dedupe depended on wording.

rejected.option: Key on the item text and the root (the round-2 plan)
rejected.why: A reworded retry reading gets new keys and queues duplicates; the test only passed because the fake reader repeated the strings.

rejected.option: Key on the closing job's own id
rejected.why: A failed-then-retried job queues each item again, so 'retrying the same job twice yields each follow-up once' fails.

rejected.option: Follow `previous_job` back to the first job
rejected.why: `previous_job` is the latest landed job in the base's history, not the retried job (chain.rs:1; scope_guard.rs:639).

rejected.option: Call `earlier_jobs` (reading/retry.rs:588)
rejected.why: It is `pub(super)`, so followups.rs cannot call it. A 16-step loop over the public `retried_job` is about ten lines.

rejected.option: Dedupe by similarity of wording across jobs
rejected.why: It needs a threshold rule and tests with no ground truth; the chain marker needs neither.

decisions.choice: `is_follow_up(item)` matches directive phrases on whole words. Normalise: lowercase, split on every character that is not alphanumeric or '-', join with single spaces. It is a follow-up when (a) the word 'as' is followed by an optional determiner (a, an, its, their) and then ('own' or 'separate') plus a noun (job, jobs, request, requests, work), or by a follow-up word (follow-up, follow-ups, followup, followups) with an optional noun; or (b) the word 'propose' or 'proposes' is followed within three words by a follow-up word, request(s) or job(s). The lists are consts. Bare 'follow-ups', 'proposal' and 'separate request' without 'as' never match.
decisions.reason: In this codebase 'follow-up', 'proposal' and 'propose' are domain words, so bare words give false positives. On this brief's own out_of_scope list none matches: 'Reprioritizing queued follow-ups ahead of or behind other work', 'Backfilling the follow-ups already lost from job ...-fgwz ...', '... a separate request from introspection ...-pj25' and the athena.toml/defaults.toml/workflows list have no 'as ...' directive and no 'propose'. 'Propose these as follow-up requests: ...' matches (a) and (b), and 'Plan critic memory runs as its own job' matches (a). It runs on an already accepted reading and is not a `check_*` step, so no reading is newly refused.

rejected.option: Bare markers (propose, follow-ups, separate request)
rejected.why: They queue the brief's own exclusions and the already-filed pj25 item.

rejected.option: Queue every out_of_scope item
rejected.why: A plain exclusion list would become a meaningless request.

rejected.option: Ask a model to classify the items
rejected.why: It adds a role and cost, and the result is not deterministic, so tests would not be reliable.

rejected.option: Match a first word 'queue' or 'propose'
rejected.why: 'Queue order and the backlog hold' is a noun phrase in the fgwz list and would queue.

decisions.choice: Build each request with `RequestQueue.apply(&ProposedChange{kind: WorkItemKind::Proposal, key, title, rung: Ladder::Implementation, source: Reference::job(<closing>), evidence: vec![Reference::job(<root>)], request: <text>, brief: None}, &taken)`. Files come only from the item. Answer to finding 4. The text is: line 1 the title (the item on one line, bullet marker stripped, cut at a whitespace boundary to about 90 chars, never mid-word); then the lines `Queued from the out_of_scope list of job <closing id>.`, `Original job: <root id>`, `Item: <item>`, `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> <n>`; then `Acceptance:` with two bullets (the named work is done with no unrelated change; fmt, clippy and test pass). Two context lines are appended only if their own text passes a per-line guard: an em dash and the root's latest reading title on the Original job line, and `Original request: <first line of the root's request, about 120 chars>`. The guard is that `followed_up_ids`, `dependency_ids_in` and `request_text_touches` find nothing in the line.
decisions.reason: `from_change` takes Files from `request_text_touches(text)` over the whole request (steward.rs:626). `request_text_touches` returns every whitespace word that `looks_like_path` accepts (a '/' or a .rs/.md/.toml/.json/.yml ending, topics.rs:63-72, 331-342). So a root title or request line that names athena.toml, and a title cut in the middle of a path, would put wrong files in the follow-up. The id-only 'Original job' line has no path word, since a job id has no '/' or those endings, so the original job is always cited. Context lines carry it only when they are clean. The item's own words are quoted as written, so Files equals `request_text_touches(item)`, or `records/` when the item names none (steward.rs:626-634: a job reference is not a path). The text never writes 'follow up', 'follow-up', 'Depends on' or 'try again on' next to an id. One request builder and one Request writer are reused: `StewardRequest::from_change` calls `StewardRequest::new` (535) and `RequestQueue::apply` (663-683) writes the record on REQUEST_CHANNEL (335). followups.rs assembles only the `ProposedChange.request` string the steward's own proposals also supply, and has no `Request {` literal and no `StewardRequest::new` call.

rejected.option: Call `StewardRequest::new` and build the `Request` record in followups.rs
rejected.why: It duplicates id generation, record writing and error mapping already in `RequestQueue::apply`, and would be a second request-text writer.

rejected.option: An explicit 'Files:' line computed from the item, with unguarded context lines
rejected.why: `from_change` still reads paths from the whole text, so context-line paths would be added anyway; the per-line guard is what removes them.

rejected.option: A new record type or marker file for follow-ups
rejected.why: The brief rules out new record types; a key line in the text is enough.

rejected.option: Write 'Follow-up from job <id>.' or add a 'Depends on <id>' line
rejected.why: The first puts 'follow-up' next to an id, which `followed_up_ids` reads as a continuation and would make the follow-up's own reading answer for the closed job. The second adds a plan edge to a closed job for no gain.

decisions.choice: Correct the assumption about the lock and the head. `follow_up_files` reads Records at `self.head()` when `close_dispatched` runs, before `land_or_block` takes `self.state.lock_repository()` (close.rs:257). The landing loop (close.rs:269-415) retries on `Refusal::Moved` and reuses `closing.files` built from the old head, as it already does for the closing records. The plan does not claim the job lock covers the dedupe check. The only writer that could add a marker for the same root between the read and the commit is another job of the same retry chain closing at the same moment. If that happens the worst case is one extra set of at most 5 requests, each visible in the ui and closed with `athena close`. Recomputing the follow-ups per attempt is not planned. Answer to finding 5.
decisions.reason: Recomputing per attempt would mean a new closure threaded through `land_or_block`, which already has ten parameters and an `allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)` (close.rs:243), plus a second call in the plain commit closure (close.rs:133-144). That is a wider edit to a file outside the reading's list. The reused files are safe across attempts: ids are generated once, and `RecordId::generate` plus the `taken` set make a collision with a record added between attempts practically impossible. A re-entry for the same job id after the 'branch kept moving' bail (close.rs:416-418) finds nothing committed, so it computes the same plan.

rejected.option: Recompute the follow-ups inside each landing attempt against that attempt's head, as `score_on` does
rejected.why: A wider close.rs edit (a new parameter on `land_or_block`) to close a race that needs two jobs of one retry chain closing at once.

rejected.option: Take the repository lock in `follow_up_files`
rejected.why: `land_or_block` takes it again at close.rs:257, and the lock is not shown to be reentrant.

decisions.choice: Name the drain-turn effect as a known consequence and pin it with a test. A follow-up is a request on REQUEST_CHANNEL, so `improvement_requests` (steward.rs:376) and `hestia::improvement_of` (hestia.rs:973-976) list it and the drain gives it the steward's guaranteed plan turn. Up to 5 follow-ups per retry chain can therefore compete for that turn. The CHANGELOG bullet says so. `followups_appear_in_queued_work_and_a_pathless_item_still_builds` asserts that `crate::hestia::improvement_of(&records).items` holds each follow-up id. Reordering is not done. Answer to finding 6.
decisions.reason: The reading requires the steward channel, so this follows from the reading, not from a plan error. The brief puts reprioritizing out of scope and hestia.rs stays unchanged. A test calling `improvement_of` from run/tests.rs reads hestia.rs and does not edit it. The behavior is pinned, not accidental, and a later request can change it with a failing test to update.

rejected.option: Queue follow-ups on a new channel so they do not get the guaranteed turn
rejected.why: The reading requires the steward channel, and `DRAINED_CHANNELS` (steward.rs:342) is outside this job's scope.

rejected.option: Say nothing and leave it unpinned
rejected.why: The critic found it has no test and is noted only in passing.

decisions.choice: Put the follow-up files in `closing.files` only; the `trailers` vector stays unchanged. `queue` is a pure function of values. Its input is the reading's items, the closing and root ids, the root's title and first request line, the texts of the existing REQUEST_CHANNEL requests, and the `taken` id set. `Athena::follow_up_files` extracts those from Records. It returns early with nothing, before loading Records, when no item passes `is_follow_up`. Any failure to read HEAD or load Records prints one ui line and returns an empty list; it never fails the close.
decisions.reason: `trailers` also feeds the landing commit message (close.rs:109-117). An `Athena-Job` trailer naming a request job whose closing records the landing does not add would refuse the landing (invariant.rs:406-422). The closing commit's own `Athena-Job` trailer already names an existing job (`names_existing_work`, invariant.rs:845-859). A pure `queue` needs no git repository or hand-built Records in unit tests, and the end-to-end tests in run/tests.rs and drain.rs cover the Records path.

rejected.option: One `Athena-Job` trailer per queued follow-up, as the steward does
rejected.why: The steward's commit is records-only; here the same vector is cloned into the landing commit, which would refuse.

rejected.option: `queue(records, reading, taken)` over `Records`
rejected.why: Unit tests would need to build `Records` by hand (many fields, store.rs:246-273).

files.purpose: The new module: MAX_PER_JOB = 5, the directive word lists, `is_follow_up`, `chain_root`, the pure `queue(..)` (chain marker, cap, request text with the per-line guard, calls `RequestQueue::apply`), `impl Athena { pub(crate) fn follow_up_files }` and the pure unit tests.
Add `pub mod followups;` between `pub mod fake;` and `pub mod gate_counts;`.

One call line in `close_dispatched` after `push_closing_records(&mut closing);` (close.rs:38). It is outside the reading's listed deliverables because it is the only place a job that ran closes (decision 1). manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are listed as deliverables but are not edited.
Add `script_with_readings(items_for)` and `script_with_out_of_scope(items)`, make `base_script()` call the latter with `["Other files"]`, and add the end-to-end tests of criteria 1-4.
Add `followups_appear_in_queued_work_after_a_job_closes` next to the queue tests (drain.rs:4783, 5410-5469), using `rated_scenario()` with its `reading["out_of_scope"]` set.
One `### Added` bullet under `[Unreleased]` for the queued follow-ups, the chain rule, the cap, the wording rule and the drain-turn effect.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/followups.rs. Define MAX_PER_JOB = 5 and the const word lists. Define `is_follow_up(item)`: lowercase, split on every character that is not alphanumeric or '-', join with single spaces; then rule (a) 'as' + optional determiner + (own|separate) + noun, or 'as' + optional determiner + follow-up word with an optional noun, and rule (b) propose|proposes within three words of a follow-up word or request(s)/job(s). Define `normalise_item` (collapse whitespace to one line, strip a leading '-', '*' or 'N.' marker, drop empty items).

In followups.rs define `chain_root(records, closing: &JobId) -> (JobId, Vec<JobId>)`: loop at most 16 times, read the current job's `request.text` from `records.jobs`, call `crate::reading::retried_job(records, text)`, stop at a cycle, an unknown job or no link; return the root and the chain. Mirror `retry_target` (preflight.rs:300-329).

In followups.rs define the pure `queue(input) -> Plan{files, jobs, skipped, already_queued}`. Input: the reading's out_of_scope items, the closing and root ids, the root's title and first request line, the texts of the existing REQUEST_CHANNEL requests, and `taken`. If any existing text has a line starting `Out-of-scope item key: <root> `, return a plan with `already_queued` and nothing else. Otherwise normalise, keep `is_follow_up` items, drop duplicates by normalised text, take the first MAX_PER_JOB and list the rest as skipped. For each, build the text of decision 5 (title cut at a whitespace boundary to about 90 chars; context lines only if `followed_up_ids`, `dependency_ids_in` and `request_text_touches` find nothing in that line), build a `ProposedChange` (kind Proposal, key, title, rung Implementation, source `Reference::job(closing)`, evidence `Reference::job(root)`, brief None), call `RequestQueue.apply(&change,&taken)` (steward.rs:660-683), add each made id to `taken`, and turn an Err into a `skipped` entry. Do not write `Request {` or call `StewardRequest::new`.

In followups.rs add `impl Athena { pub(crate) fn follow_up_files(&self, closing: &JobId, reading: &Reading, ui: &dyn Ui) -> Vec<NewFile> }`. Return early with nothing when no item passes `is_follow_up`. Otherwise load `Records` at `self.head()` (lib.rs:273), compute `chain_root` for `closing`, collect the request texts on REQUEST_CHANNEL and the root's title and request line, call `queue`, print one ui line per queued item, one for 'already queued for <root>' and one per skipped item (cap of 5, refused text), and return the files. A failure to read HEAD or load Records prints one line and returns an empty list; it never fails the close.

Add `pub mod followups;` to crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs between `fake` and `gate_counts`. In crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs add `closing.files.extend(self.follow_up_files(ctx.id(), ctx.reading, ctx.ui));` after `push_closing_records(&mut closing);` (line 38). Do not touch `trailers`, `commit_hold`, `land_or_block` or the landing loop. Do not edit manage.rs, steward.rs or reading.rs unless a compile error shows a need, and say so in the report.

In crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs add `script_with_readings(items_for: impl Fn(usize) -> Vec<String> + Send + Sync + 'static) -> athena_agent::fake::Script`: the body of `base_script()` with `"out_of_scope"` taken from `items_for(n)`, where `n` counts reader invocations with an `AtomicUsize` inside the closure. Add `script_with_out_of_scope(items: &[&str])` over it, and make `base_script()` call `script_with_out_of_scope(&["Other files"])`. Then add the end-to-end tests named in the demonstrations: `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_of_a_closed_job` (with a prior `ask`ed job, an intervention commit and a shared `Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>` of items); `followups_ignore_plain_exclusions_and_an_empty_out_of_scope_on_close`; `followups_are_queued_once_on_reclose`; `followups_are_queued_once_across_a_failed_job_and_its_retry` (FAILS_ON_EDIT, the retry's reading worded differently); `followups_are_queued_once_when_a_held_job_is_retried` (modelled on run/tests.rs:4390-4401); `followups_appear_in_queued_work_and_a_pathless_item_still_builds` (with the `improvement_of` assertion).

Write the unit tests in followups.rs: `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_pure` (a table of this brief's six real out_of_scope items, which expect no request, and the fgwz-shaped directives including the one citing two ids, which expect one each); `followups_ignore_plain_exclusions_and_an_empty_out_of_scope_pure`; `followups_are_queued_once_and_capped_pure` (second call, reworded second call, 7 items to 5, repeated item); `followups_files_come_from_the_item_only_pure` (root title and request line naming paths, an item whose path word sits at the 90-char cut, a pathless item gives `records/`); `followups_text_is_a_reference_not_a_dependency_pure` (including a root title that says 'follow up on job <id>'); `followups_reword_banned_words_pure` (words built at run time from `boundary_words()` and `boundary_fragments()`).

In crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs add `followups_appear_in_queued_work_after_a_job_closes`: `rated_scenario()`, set `scenario.reading["out_of_scope"]`, `fx.athena(scenario.script())`, `athena.queue(FIRST)`, `athena.go(..)` twice as `a_running_job_stays_out_of_the_queue` does (drain.rs:5459-5462), then assert `queued_ids(&fx)` holds the follow-up ids and not the original job.

Add the CHANGELOG.md bullet under `### Added` in `[Unreleased]`, copying the neighbouring bullets' form: the follow-ups are queued as their own steward requests citing the original job, the wording that tells them from plain exclusions, the cap of 5 and once per retry chain, and the known effect that they get the drain's guaranteed improvement turn. Change no existing line.

Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. Fix what fails without loosening any test. If the gate refuses the closing commit that carries the request files, or a scope guard refuses the close.rs edit, report it instead of weakening a rule.

risks.risk: A retry whose reading adds a genuinely new follow-up queues none of it, because the chain marker from the first job's close stops all later jobs of the chain (decision 3).
risks.mitigation: This is the trade the finding asked for: wording drift would otherwise duplicate every request. The ui line for a close that finds a marker says 'already queued for <root>', so a person can queue the new item by hand. The cap of 5 per chain bounds the other direction.

risks.risk: The directive phrases can still queue an item that is really an exclusion (for example 'treat the proposal as its own request'), and one that merely cites an existing job is now queued too.
risks.mitigation: Whole-word directive matching, the cap of 5, the chain marker and a ui line per queued request. The word lists are two consts covered by the table test, and a wrong request is closed with `athena close`.

risks.risk: Follow-ups get the drain's guaranteed improvement turn (hestia.rs:973-976 treats every open REQUEST_CHANNEL request as one of Athena's own), so up to 5 per chain compete with user work.
risks.mitigation: The reading requires the steward channel, so this follows from the reading. It is named in the CHANGELOG bullet and pinned by the `improvement_of` assertion in `followups_appear_in_queued_work_and_a_pathless_item_still_builds`. Reordering is out of scope.

risks.risk: Concurrent closes of two jobs of the same retry chain could each queue a set, since the dedupe read happens before the repository lock (close.rs:257) and the landing loop reuses the files on `Refusal::Moved`.
risks.mitigation: The job lock is not claimed. The worst case is one extra set of at most 5 requests, visible in the ui and closed with `athena close`. A retry normally starts after its target has closed.

risks.risk: The closing commit now adds job directories that hold only a request.json. A gate rule, the history check or `athena check` could object when the closing commit is not the steward's.
risks.mitigation: `closing_jobs` counts only candidate, verification and outcome files (invariant.rs:240-269) and `landing` checks only the landed job (386-446). The end-to-end test commits through the real gate on a branch with an intervention commit. If the gate refuses, the producer reports it and does not weaken a rule.

risks.risk: A queued text could be read by `followed_up_ids` as continuing the original job, and the follow-up's own reading would then be refused when the drain reads it. An item that itself says 'follow up on job <id>' is quoted as written and has that effect.
risks.mitigation: The generated lines write no follow-up phrase before an id, and the context lines are included only when the three finders find nothing in them. A unit test asserts the three finders return nothing on each queued text, with a hostile root title. The item's own words are the model's, so they get the same reading any request with that wording gets.

risks.risk: When an item cites three or more ids, `referenced_jobs` carries only the first 3 in text order (topics.rs:546-548), so the original job may not be shown to the follow-up's reader as evidence, though its id stays in the text.
risks.mitigation: The item is the first line, so cited ids come first and the original job is cited on later lines; the id stays in the text for a reader to follow. This is truncation, never a refusal. Not worth a rule for a case the fgwz list does not show.

risks.risk: The Files line falls back to `records/` when the item names no path, and a reader may treat `records/` as a governance area.
risks.mitigation: This is the brief's stated fallback and matches `from_change` (steward.rs:626-634). The reader makes its own deliverable list, so Files is a hint, not a limit.

risks.risk: run/close.rs is outside the reading's listed deliverables, while manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are listed and left unedited.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one call line and the logic is in followups.rs. The code shows manage.rs is not the close path for a job that ran (decision 1). If a scope guard refuses the close.rs edit, the producer reports it and does not route around it.

risks.risk: Test fixtures need words from the boundary lists, and the boundary scan fails any tracked file that names them.
risks.mitigation: Tests build them at run time from `athena_context::briefs::boundary_words()` and `boundary_fragments()`, as briefs.rs:2369 does; `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` runs in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: Loading Records at HEAD adds cost to a close.
risks.mitigation: `follow_up_files` returns before loading when no out_of_scope item passes `is_follow_up`; `score_on` already loads Records at HEAD per closing attempt (close.rs:24).

demonstrations.observes: One added bullet. It says: when a job ends with a reading, each out_of_scope item that names separate work (wording such as 'as its own job', 'as a follow-up request' or 'propose ... follow-up') is queued as its own steward request citing the original job; items that only list files or rules are told apart by that wording and queue nothing. It queues at most 5 per job and its retries, and once per retry chain whatever the later wording. It says the requests are on the steward channel and so get the drain's guaranteed improvement turn and can compete with user work, a known effect (finding 6). A repeated close, a retry or a resume queues nothing new.

demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `close_dispatched` call, `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_of_a_closed_job` fails and `cargo test --locked` exits non-zero. A line over rustfmt width in followups.rs, or an unused const (MAX_PER_JOB or a word list left unused), makes `cargo fmt --all --check` or `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` exit non-zero. If `pub mod followups;` is missing from lib.rs, its tests are not built and the criterion 1-4 filters match nothing. If the `base_script()` change altered its default reading, existing tests in run/tests.rs would fail.
demonstrations.seam: The three check commands Athena runs (listed under 'Checks Athena will run'). The seam exists today; no plan step adds it.
